notes.rule: spec/stale-statement
notes.claim: the README says the reports and holidays E2E suites are ones "this area does not touch and which must stay green"; the holidays E2E suite pins the very rule REQ-01-026 drops and cannot stay green untouched

witness.detail: e2e/tests/holidays.spec.ts:296-338 (TC-03-E2E-04) seeds a holiday with countryCode 'BY', calls setOwnCountryViaApi(request, 'BY') at :309 — which writes Account.phoneCountryCode — and then asserts `time-cell-{day}-holiday-marker` is visible on the weekly calendar. Under REQ-01-026 that member has no Membership.countryCode and the organization has none either, so the chain resolves null, GET /holidays?scope=mine returns global rows only, and the marker is not drawn. Three integration cases are in the same position: apps/api/test/holidays.spec.ts:381 (fixture at :402), apps/api/test/reports-amounts-owed.spec.ts:573 and :607, and apps/api/test/reports-time-off.spec.ts:404.

notes.rule: spec/ambiguous-requirement
notes.claim: whether a two-letter code that is not an assigned ISO country ('XX') is accepted by the two country writes has two readings

witness.detail: PUT /api/organizations/{orgId}/settings/country with { "countryCode": "XX" }. REQ-01-036 refuses anything "neither empty nor a valid alpha-2 value", and Edge case 10 defines "XX" as a value that does not normalize to a valid alpha-2 value — so 422. The contracts' Validation Rule 9 states the constraint as "Empty, or exactly 2 uppercase letters" and the note under the table says the rule is the one "the holiday rows' country validator already does", which is validateHolidayCountryCode (packages/validation/src/holidays.ts:93, test /^[A-Z]{2}$/) — so 200. No case exercises it.

notes.suggestedFix: one clause saying whether the write checks membership of the ISO list or only the two-uppercase-letters shape. Planned as the Validation Rules table states it (validateHolidayCountryCode on both writes), since that table is the normative statement of what each write refuses and the read side skips a stored 'XX' regardless (REQ-01-027)

notes.rule: spec/untestable-case
notes.claim: the case says a user and a viewer "receive the identical body" from the member detail read, and the shipped projection carries caller-dependent fields, so a literal reading of that clause cannot pass

witness.detail: MembersService.getDetail returns callerRole, canEditRole and availableRoles (apps/api/src/members/members.service.ts:352-374); callerRole is 'user' for one caller and 'viewer' for the other, so a deep-equality assertion between the two bodies fails on a field this spec does not touch. The rest of the sentence says what is meant — "field included: the read is gated by no capability and the field is not conditional on one".

notes.suggestedFix: narrow the clause to the field the case is about. Planned as: countryCode present and equal for both callers, alongside the target-derived fields; no product code differs between the two readings

notes.rule: reviewer — two writes of one field disagree on what an absent key means, and only one of them wrote the decision down
notes.claim: on the organization country PUT an absent countryCode key clears the stored value, while the member update beside it deliberately treats an absent key as no submission at all

witness.detail: An admin has stored PL. A caller sends PUT /api/organizations/{orgId}/settings/country with body {}. organization-country.service.ts:69 evaluates validateHolidayCountryCode(undefined), which returns { valid: true, value: null } (packages/validation/src/holidays.ts:96), and the update writes countryCode: null. The response is 200 {"countryCode":null} and every member relying on the organization link drops to global holidays only. REQ-01-034 speaks only of a caller who 'submits an empty country'; it does not say an absent key is a submission. The member write chose the opposite reading and recorded it in the code — members.service.ts, the wantsCountry branch: 'the key's presence — not its value — decides'. Left as a note because the screen always sends the key and the two routes differ in shape (a single-field PUT against a multi-field one), so nothing reachable through the product hits it.

notes.suggestedFix: either apply the same presence-decides rule here, or record in the contract that an absent key clears the column, so the difference between the two writes is a stated decision rather than a by-product of a shared validator

notes.rule: spec/incomplete-decision
notes.claim: neither the requirements nor the contracts say what an absent countryCode key means on either country write, and the two routes have been given opposite answers by their shipped implementations

notes.rule: sweep 8 — a test that fails for a reason other than the rule it guards
notes.symbol: picking four people holds through every window preset and step
notes.claim: the new week-start assertion computes the expected Monday from the runner's UTC clock while the screen computes its anchor in the account's Europe/Berlin zone — the browser-clock/account-zone split F2 was raised about, reintroduced inside the assertion that guards it

witness.detail: signupOrg seeds the account with timezone 'Europe/Berlin' (e2e/tests/helpers.ts:138). The screen's anchor is timeOffCalendarToday('Europe/Berlin'); the test takes new Date() at line 279, reduces it to the runner's UTC calendar date and steps back to that date's Monday. On a Sunday between 22:00 and 23:59 UTC under CEST the account is already on Monday while the runner is still on Sunday, so the screen renders the week beginning that Monday and the assertion expects calendar-day-header-<previous Monday>: the case fails against correct code. Nothing else in the case is time-dependent — the day-header counts at 274 and 277 hold in every zone.

notes.suggestedFix: derive the expected Monday from the account's zone the way the screen does, or assert the first header's weekday label rather than its date
